headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading workflow errors between Kestra and Prefect.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can read/write files and expose stdin/stdout plus workflow artifacts, while Prefect can consume workflow metadata and broad egress. A shared workspace or copy-paste bridge could let Kestra-produced content influence Prefect, but no direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or file tree
IF Prefect ingests Kestra-generated files or stdout as instructions
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Disable automatic parsing of agent output as workflow instructions
Add a manual review step before Prefect consumes Kestra artifacts
Use read-only mounts for any shared inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and has broad network egress; Prefect also has broad egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive workflow data can flow from Kestra into Prefect outputs or remote services. The pairwise path is plausible in default orchestration setups, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Kestra and Prefect share files, secrets, or the same runtime identity
IF either agent forwards workflow contents to external APIs or notifications
mitigations: Remove shared secrets from both runtimes
Restrict outbound network destinations
Store sensitive artifacts in separate buckets per agent
Review logs for accidental payload capture
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra can execute shell, spawn subprocesses, read/write the filesystem, and request root/docker.sock; Prefect has broad egress and can operate on workflow metadata. If both are run against the same mutable workspace, Kestra's write and execution powers can collide with Prefect's orchestration state, creating destructive race conditions. Uncertainty about locking pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git checkout
IF orchestration state is mutated without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Run only one writer per resource at a time
Make shared inputs read-only
Pause one agent during stateful updates
requires-engineering: add distributed locks around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can emit workflow outputs, logs, and notifications, and Prefect can consume workflow metadata. That makes it plausible for Prefect to treat Kestra output as authoritative and propagate mistakes into downstream actions. Because the pair lacks documented verification or provenance controls, the cascade risk is high rather than medium.
conditions: IF Prefect uses Kestra-produced metadata or artifacts as trusted inputs
IF downstream tasks act on those inputs without validation
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require human approval for high-impact outputs
Compare outputs against source-of-truth records
Limit downstream actions to dry-run mode
requires-engineering: add schema and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source data-engineering tools with no explicit residency, certification, or retention claims. The only concrete compliance concern is that Kestra handles broader data classes than Prefect, so a mismatch could arise if regulated data is routed through both. With no documented residency or certification conflict, this remains low.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents
IF one agent's logging or retention policy is stricter than the other's
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through the pair
Minimize logged payload contents
Set short retention on both systems
Review deployment region settings
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-handling policy parity
